reason: The cited evidence confirms the lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure (E2) and that spinel oxides form on a related HEA at high temperature (E4), but no evidence supports oxide formation specifically on the fcc phase at 700 °C, its preferential mechanical removal, or the claimed galvanic coupling between fcc and B2. E5 describes pitting on Al-Ni-rich phases in a different solution without wear, and E1 is irrelevant to the degradation mechanism.
premises: A protective oxide film forms on the fcc phase at 700 °C
The oxide on the softer fcc phase is mechanically removed by wear, especially at phase boundaries
Exposed fcc regions become anodic relative to the nobler B2 phase
Galvanic coupling between fcc and B2 enhances localized corrosion
Refining lamellar spacing reduces phase boundary area and thus degradation
